title: Lemon Curd
subtitle: Thick, buttery, intensely sharp lemon curd
excerpt: Lemon curd is eggs, butter, sugar, and lemon juice cooked slowly until thick. It keeps 4 weeks in the fridge. Makes two small jars, it's a refrigerator preserve, not a shelf-stable one.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Lemon curd is a Victorian British preserve made in small quantities due to its refrigerator shelf life.

recipe.freezeNotes: Lemon curd freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost slowly in the fridge and stir before using.

glossaryTerms.definition: A heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, so the steam heats the bowl gently. Used for delicate emulsions like curd and custard where direct heat would scramble the eggs.

content.text: Lemon curd is a butter-thickened egg preserve,  sharp, rich, and spreadable. It goes on scones, toast, and sponge layers, and inside meringues. The fridge shelf life is 4 weeks, which is why it's made in small batches. Makes about two 200 g jars.
or a very gentle direct heat,  too hot and the eggs scramble. Patience is the whole skill: keep the heat low and stir constantly, and the curd will thicken smoothly.

Put the lemon juice, zest, sugar, and butter in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water. The base of the bowl should not touch the water. Stir until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.
Add the eggs and cook until thick

Add the beaten eggs to the bowl and stir constantly with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula. Keep the heat under the water at a low simmer,  it should not bubble hard. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring without stopping, until the curd thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and holds a clear line when you run your finger across it.
Pour through a fine sieve into the hot sterilised jars to catch the zest and any cooked egg strands. Seal and leave to cool. The curd will thicken further as it cools.

items.symptom: Curd is grainy or has scrambled specks
items.cause: Heat was too high, the eggs partially cooked rather than thickening slowly.
items.fix: Strain through a fine sieve to remove the grains. The flavour is usually fine. Next time keep the water at a bare simmer, not a boil.

items.symptom: Curd is too runny even when cold
items.cause: Not cooked long enough to thicken fully.
items.fix: Return to the double boiler and cook for another 10 minutes. The curd continues to thicken significantly as it cools.

items.cause: Too many whole eggs relative to yolks.
items.fix: The extra yolk in this recipe helps. For a richer, less eggy curd, use 2 whole eggs and 3 yolks instead.

items.cause: Commercial lemon juice is less sharp than fresh-squeezed.
items.fix: Always use freshly squeezed lemon juice. Increase lemon juice to 120 ml for a sharper result.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Keeps for 4 weeks in the fridge. Freeze for up to 3 months.
